 White Sox Trade Jordan Leasure To Phillies
 By Anthony Franco |
 at November 20, 2026 4:34pm CDT 
 The White Sox have traded reliever  Jordan Leasure to the Phillies for minor league pitcher Christian Coppola , according to announcements from both clubs. Philadelphia immediately agreed to a deal with Leasure to avoid arbitration.
 Leasure was designated for assignment earlier in the week when Chicago signed  Dustin May . He’s a couple months removed from undergoing UCL surgery that’ll likely cost him all of 2027. The Phils need to carry him on their offseason 40-man roster but can place him on the 60-day injured list at the beginning of Spring Training.
 The 28-year-old Leasure had a productive 2025 season. He tossed 64 1/3 innings of 3.92 ERA ball and led White Sox relievers with 80 strikeouts. He worked his way into leverage spots and picked up seven saves. Leasure wasn’t nearly as effective this year, allowing 14 runs across 18 2/3 innings and spending a couple weeks on optional assignment to Triple-A. He’s likely making around the league minimum salary — MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz had projected him at $1MM — and has three additional years of arbitration control.
 Philadelphia takes a reclamation flier, parting with their 12th round pick from this year’s draft. Coppola, who stands 6’5″, is a local product whom the Phils nabbed out of St. Joseph’s University. He hasn’t pitched professionally but recorded 69 strikeouts across 37 1/3 innings against small-school competition as a senior. Baseball America rated him the #326 player in this year’s draft, praising the movement he generates on his sweeping slider.
